title: John’s Significant Other Ded Reckin with White Industries Desert Sage – John Watson
content:
When John first saw Ashley King from Significant Other’s Ded Reckin prototype at the 2025 Made Bike Show, he told her he’d buy one. Last December, Ashley opened a pre-order for the titanium-and-steel 120/130 bike, prompting him to buy one. Now, eight months later, his build is finished, featuring limited-edition Desert Sage White Industries hubs, a matching Cerakote swingarm, Cane Creek Coil IL coil, and logos. Let’s check it out!

Ded Reckin

It is no secret that I’m a huge metal fan. I love metal full-suspension bikes. Having ridden and owned several since 2018, I know what I like. And when I saw Ashley King’s Ded Reckin prototype last year at Made, it checked a lot of boxes. It was my favorite bike at the framebuilder show, and when she opened pre-orders, I looked at the DR-51 (XL) frame geometry and immediately put down a deposit.

I’m a big guy, so seeing the head tube length (150 mm), effective top tube (674 mm), and chainstay length (450 mm!) on the biggest size (DR-51) Ded Reckin made my mouth froth. Finally, someone gets it. There’s something reassuring when a company hears your cries for big-guy geometry.

After Paul’s review of the Ded Reckin and Travis’s interview with Ashley from Sea Otter this year, I couldn’t contain myself any longer. The anticipation was real!

Speaking of, if you want to dive deeper into who Ashley King is, the Ded Reckin, and more, peep our Archives:

  • Inside / Out at Significant Other Bikes
  • 2025 Made Bike Show: Significant Other Ded Reckin Titanium Full Suspension
  • Ashley King Of Significant Other Bikes On Fulfilling The Doom Scroll Prophecy … and Your Ded Reckin Pre-Orders
  • Significant Other Ded Reckin Review: Free Thy Eye

Tan Man

A few months later, Heather McFadden, in her new role at White Industries, emailed me about a forthcoming limited-edition Desert Sage run of components the brand would debut this summer. The White Industries Desert Sage hubs are right up my alley, as Mr. Earthtone, aka Tan Man, and the Ded Reckin would be the perfect bike to pair them with.

Ashley, Heather, and I got on an email chain and made it happen. Last month, the wheels and frame showed up, and I spent an afternoon assembling it from a mix of old and new parts. With a torque wrench, Enduro tools, and titanium grease in hand, it came together bit by bit. Ashley did a phenomenal job prepping the frame, so it was easy for this at-home mechanic to build it up without fuss.

If you really want to get to know a frame, build it up yourself. Most of the time, I don’t have the time or capacity to build review bikes, so I drop them off at one of my local shops for the build. For this bike, however, I really wanted to get intimate with it. Once the frame showed up – after being lost in UPS purgatory for a week – the parts were all laid out, ready to be hung on the frame.

Components

The folks at White Industries graciously sent over their new cranks, along with a 28-tooth polished ring, bottom bracket, headset, and seat collar. Loren at Astral oversaw the wheel build. Those Serpentine rims I love so much, laced to the Desert Sage White Industries hubs.  Without their contribution, this build wouldn’t have been possible, so a huge thanks to Alec, Heather, and Loren for their help!

I worked with Steve Ziegler, who helped Ashley design the Ded Rek, on the appropriate coil spec. Since this bike’s kinematics are progressive, we went with a Cane Creek Coil IL shock featuring a 650-lb linear coil. Steve sent over a few charts along with his recommendation, and I trusted his guidance. Hey, why not get that coil Cerakoted to match? Sick.

It came together beautifully. Massive thanks to Wolf Tooth for the custom laser-engraved CTRL pedals, too!

To match the drivetrain, a Madrone Jab with the new MTB clutch has a black SRAM Eagle chain wrapped around a Garbaruk silver cassette. The wheels are wrapped in Schwalbe Romy Soft casing tires, 2.5″, and stopping power is assisted by Hope centerlock rotors, held in place by Ogle lockrings, with my Trickstuff Piccola brakes.

Speaking of the brakes, the cockpit features an Ogle stem, Ti Doom Lucky Riser handlebars, Ergon team GDH grips, and an Eagle GX shifter with a Wolf Tooth dropper that activates the 225 mm PNW Loam Dropper. My saddle height is 83 cm in these photos, and Ashley exclaimed, “I’m glad I made your seat tube longer!” when seeing the initial build photos.

Ded Reckin Overforked

I snagged a Manitou Mattoc Pro after enjoying the fork on my Murmur all year, and I didn’t realize it was a 140 mm fork until I installed it. Once again, I consulted Steve, and he assured me the bike would jam with a 140 mm travel fork and not fret. And if I want to ride it with a 130, the travel change is a cinch with the Mattoc Pro. I bought this bike to have a trail bruiser, my Murmur, at 135/160, and a “downcountry” bike like the Ded Reckin at 120/130, so I’ll probably end up changing the travel down after the Made Bike Show. My time on the Sour Cowboy Cookie solidified my love for 120/130 metal bikes.

More to Come?

I’ll put in some miles on the bike this fall, and I’m sure it’ll make a few more appearances on The Radavist over the following years. Paul’s review is superb, and I couldn’t add anything else to his assessment of the bike. Hell, I haven’t even ridden it yet! It’s gotta stay clean through this weekend.

Speaking of, my Ded Reckin will be on display at the White Industries and Astral booth at this weekend’s Made Bike Show, so be sure to check it out because it’s not gonna stay this clean for long!

I wanted to thank Ashley King for making a bike that is literally from my dreams, and Steve Ziegler for the assist on the kinematics layout. Metal full suspensions are really special. The Ded Reckin went from being my favorite bike at the 2025 Made Bike Show to my personal build being on display at the 2026 Made Bike Show.

Supporting small builders and makers is a lifelong pursuit of mine, and this Ded Reckin is a shining example of the talent found across the United States (and beyond) in workshops where passion is milled into products.

See you at the 2026 Made Bike Show. Check the bike out at the White Industries and Astral booth, and be sure to swing by The Radavist’s booth, right next to Shimano. Come say hey and chat with our team!

Build Spec:

  • Frame: Significant Other Ded Reckin XL
  • Fork: Manitou Mattoc Pro
  • Shock: Cane Creek Coil IL 650 lb Linear Coil
  • Hubs: White Industries Desert Sage
  • Rims: Astral Serpentine
  • Headset: White Industries
  • Collar: White Industries
  • Cranks: White Industries Ti
  • Bottom bracket: White Industries
  • Derailleur: Madrone Jab
  • Cassette: Garbaruk
  • Chain: SRAM Eagle 12
  • Pedals: Radavist engraved Wolf Tooth CTRL
  • Stem: Ogle Ti
  • Bars: Doom Ti Lucky Riser
  • Brakes: Trickstuff Piccola HD
  • Shifter: Eagle GX
  • Dropper Lever: Wolf Tooth
  • Grips: Ergon GDH Team
  • Rotors: Hope Centerlock
  • CL Ring: Ogle
  • Tires: Schwalbe Radial Romy Soft 2.5″
  • Valves: Wolf Tooth
  • Dropper: PNW Loam Gen 2 225 mm
  • Saddle: Ergon Enduro Ti

Ashley is opening another pre-order for the Ded Reckin this fall. Sign up for updates via her newsletter on the Significant Other Bikes website.

Many thanks to White Industries and Astral for sending out parts for the build. I bought all other components from my local shop or pulled them from my parts bin. Check out the Desert Sage collection at White Industries.
